class.name: UZUPBRFromImage
class.brief_description: Makes estimated PBR maps and a material from one texture image.
class.description: [UZUPBRFromImage] turns one texture image into estimated PBR maps and an [ORMMaterial3D] that uses them: - Albedo: the image with the slow, baked-in light gradient taken out. - Normal: from the height, in the OpenGL convention (green = up), as Godot expects. - ORM: ambient occlusion (red), roughness (green), metallic (blue). - Height: bright = high (mortar and cracks are dark), stretched to 0..1. Each kind of material (see [method get_kinds]) has its own normal strength, roughness, metallic and share of fine detail. These were fitted against scanned materials. [b]Note:[/b] The maps are estimated, not scanned. A normal map guessed from brightness is about as far from a scan as a flat normal map is: dark stains read as holes. For a better normal map, bring one from an outside model in with [UZUMapImport] and pass it as the [code]normal[/code] option. [b]Note:[/b] This class is specific to U.ZU Engine (U.ZU Picture).

method.name: compare
method.description: Compares a normal map with a reference one, such as a scan. Both are scaled to 256x256. The result has [code]normal_angle_error_deg[/code] (the mean angle between the two) and [code]flat_normal_error_deg[/code] (the same for a flat normal map), so the two numbers show whether the map is better than nothing. With [param orm] and [param reference_orm] (ORM or ARM maps), it also has [code]roughness_mean[/code], [code]ref_roughness_mean[/code] and [code]roughness_correlation[/code] (from the green channels).

method.name: get_kinds
method.description: Returns the kinds of material, each with [code]strength[/code] (normal strength), [code]rough[/code] (base roughness), [code]spread[/code] (how much roughness varies), [code]metal[/code] and [code]detail[/code] (the share of fine grain in the height). The kinds are stone, brick, cobble, ground, wood, plaster, fabric, leather, metal and painted_metal.

method.name: make
method.description: Makes the maps from [param image]. The [param options] are: - [code]strength[/code] (1.0): multiplies the kind's normal strength. - [code]delight[/code] (0.7): how much of the baked light gradient to take out, from 0 to 1. - [code]tile[/code] (false): the texture repeats, so blurs and slopes wrap around the edges. - [code]invert[/code] (false): dark is high. - [code]size[/code] (1024): the largest width; wider images are scaled down. - [code]normal[/code]: an [Image] to use as the normal map instead of the estimate. The result has [code]ok[/code], [code skip-lint]kind[/code], [code skip-lint]size[/code], the images [code]albedo[/code], [code]normal[/code], [code]orm[/code] and [code]height[/code], [code]material[/code] (an [ORMMaterial3D]), [code]normal_source[/code], [code]stats[/code] ([code]roughness_mean[/code], [code]normal_strength[/code], [code]baked_light_range[/code], [code]seam[/code]) and [code]warnings[/code]. The warnings cover strong baked light and edges that will show seams when repeated. On failure, the result has [code]error[/code].

method.name: make_file
method.description: Does [method make] on the image at [param in_path], then writes [code]albedo.png[/code], [code]normal.png[/code], [code]orm.png[/code], [code]height.png[/code] and [code]material.tres[/code] into [param out_dir]. The material keeps its textures inside, so it works without an import step. The [param options] are those of [method make], plus [code]normal_from[/code], a path to a normal map. The result has [code]files[/code] instead of the images and the material.
